newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures hold gains after benign CPI data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures hold gains after benign CPI data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures held sharp gains which were set after U.S. consumer prices stayed in check in March.

June T-bonds outperformed Eurodollars, gapping nearly a point higher in reaction to the much-awaited Consumer Price Index (CPI), which increased 0.2 percent in the core rate and rose 0.1 percent overall.
Dealers and firms, on average, were expecting a rise of 0.2 percent overall and 0.3 percent in the core rate.
Most bond futures traders said the market had been pricing in a rise of 0.4 percent in the core rate.
"As soon as the number came out, everyone knew what was going to happen," a bond futures analyst said. "There was just too much demand and no supply between 107-00 and 107-15/32."
June bonds rose to 107-21/32, and tested that level about an hour and a half after the pit opened.
Some traders look for the relief rally to carry June T-bonds to 107-26/32 to 107-28/32, while one floor trader said a rally to 108-16/32 later in the session would not be far-fetched.
"We forced a lot of shorts to cover positions," he said. "And that could continue to the 108-16/32 area."
Many traders had noted that Friday's sell-off was marked by a sharp increase in total open interest and a seven-month low in the June bond contract.
Meanwhile, Eurodollars stalled, finding little follow-through buying, a Eurodollar futures trader said.
He said the U.S. consumer price data were "surprising," particularly housing prices which were unchanged from February.
"Those numbers seem seriously flawed," he said. "But this is a backward-looking report."

However, bond and Eurodollar traders said both markets were poised for further declines. One bond trader said June would have to rise to 109-25/32 before speculation about a intermediate-term bottom took root.
"This is not a rally that has changed the trend by any stretch of the imagination," he said. "The weight of data indicating that the economy is growing faster than the Fed wants is too overwhelming."

At 0903 CDT/1403 GMT, June T-bonds were up 29/32 at 107-19/32, notes were 17/32 higher at 105-25/32, September T-bills were up 0.045 at 94.28 and September Eurodollars were up 0.55 at 93.70. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
